instructions.5: Serve the rolls in a bowl with thin rice noodles, chopped lettuce, and assorted Vietnamese herbs. Top with roasted peanuts and a Vietnamese fish sauce dipping sauce. You can also serve the rolls with rice paper on the side for a more self-assembly dish.

w-vn-002.culturalNotes: Grilled beef in betel leaves is a traditional Vietnamese dish often served on special occasions.

w-vn-003.title: Pandan Waffles (Bánh Kếp Lá Dứa)

instructions.1: Melt the butter in the microwave on Low power for 30-45 seconds. Stir to combine and allow to cool.
instructions.2: In a large measuring cup or mixing bowl, sift together the rice flour, tapioca starch, all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt.
instructions.3: In a large mixing bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar until mostly combined. Add the coconut milk, melted butter, and pandan paste. Whisk together until well combined.
instructions.4: Add half of the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and combine until mostly incorporated. Add the remaining dry ingredients and continue whisking gently, breaking up the bigger lumps. Let the batter rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.5: Set the waffle maker to the 'Max' or highest setting and heat until hot. Pour about 2/3 cup of batter into the waffle maker. Using a spatula or spoon, spread the batter evenly over the peaks of the waffle maker. Close the lid and cook for 4-5 minutes until golden brown.
instructions.6: Use a bamboo skewer to lift a section of the waffle and then use tongs to remove and transfer to a wire cooling rack.
instructions.7: Serve the waffles hot.

w-vn-003.culturalNotes: Pandan waffles (Bánh Kếp Lá Dứa) are a traditional Vietnamese dessert known for their aromatic pandan and coconut milk flavors.

w-vn-004.title: Bánh pía

instructions.1: Mix the flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
instructions.2: Add the eggs, milk, and vegetable oil and mix the ingredients well until the dough is smooth.
instructions.3: Cover the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Divide the dough into 12 equal pieces and shape each piece into a ball.
instructions.5: Add the filling to the center of each ball and wrap it with the dough.
instructions.6: Place the ball in Bánh pía molds and put them in a preheated oven at 180 degrees Celsius.
instructions.7: Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

w-vn-004.culturalNotes: Bánh pía is a traditional Vietnamese pastry, often served on special occasions.

w-vn-005.title: Vietnamese Rice Paper Salad (Bánh Tráng Trộn)

instructions.1: If using tamarind pulp, soak it in 2 cups of hot water for 15 minutes, then strain through a fine sieve and discard the pulp.
instructions.2: In a small saucepan, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and sauté until fragrant (about 15 seconds). Add the tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, MSG, and red pepper flakes. Mix until combined. Cook on low simmer for 1 minute. Pour into a small bowl and set aside.
instructions.3: In a medium skillet, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Add the dried squid to the hot oil and fry for 30 seconds. The squid will curl, so use chopsticks or a wooden spoon to push down the sides to prevent curling and ensure even frying. Flip and fry the other side for another 30 seconds. Remove from the oil. Once cooled, hand shred the squid into long strips and set aside.
instructions.4: In the same oil, add the dried shrimp. Pan fry for about 1 minute. Remove from the oil and set aside.
instructions.5: For the beef jerky, hand shred it into thin strips and set aside.
instructions.6: Place the rice paper in a large bowl. Add the tamarind sauce, chili oil, and scallion oil. Toss the rice paper evenly so it soaks up all the sauces. It will appear dry at first, but it will soften.
instructions.7: Add the proteins (beef jerky, dried squid, and dried shrimp), green mango, and hard-boiled quail eggs. Give it a quick mix.
instructions.8: Garnish with fried shallots, peanuts, and Vietnamese coriander.

w-vn-005.culturalNotes: Vietnamese Rice Paper Salad (Bánh Tráng Trộn) is a popular dish in Vietnam, served as an appetizer or a light meal.

w-vn-006.title: Chè Trôi Nước (Vietnamese Glutinous Rice Balls in Ginger Syrup)

instructions.1: In a large mixing bowl, combine glutinous rice flour and hot water. Mix and knead until you get a smooth dough. Do not add more water. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Once the dough has rested, divide the dough mixture into 28 balls, about 1 inch in diameter.
instructions.3: Rinse the peeled mung beans until the water runs clear. In a medium pan, add the rinsed mung beans and enough water to cover them by 1 inch. Cook over medium heat until it boils, then reduce the heat and continue cooking until the beans are softened but still maintain their shape (about 15 minutes). Monitor the pot carefully and reduce the heat as needed to prevent it from boiling over. Drain the beans and return them to the stove with the heat off to evaporate any residual moisture. Add salt and sugar. Then use a large spoon to smash and mix them into a rough paste. It doesn’t need to be smooth.
instructions.4: Roll the filling into small balls, about ½ inch in diameter (about 28 pieces). If you find that the mixture is too soft to handle, chill it in the fridge.
instructions.5: Flatten the mochi wrapper ball into a thick disc. Place a mung bean filling ball in the center. Fold the dough over to close, gently encasing the filling by rolling it back and forth in your palm into a smooth ball. Be careful not to let the mung bean filling spill out of the wrapper, as cooking it will cause the filling to leak and the ball to fall apart. Use any leftover dough to form small pearls without filling. Once you’re done, cover and set aside to prevent drying.
instructions.6: In a large pot, boil water with the palm sugar until sugar dissolves. Use a spoon to peel the ginger and cut into matchstick-sized strips. Gently drop the dough balls into the syrup. Simmer gently on medium-low heat until they float (about 20 minutes).
instructions.7: Make the coconut milk sauce if desired.
instructions.8: Scoop a few cooked rice balls with syrup into a bowl. Drizzle with the coconut sauce. Top with roasted sesame seeds. Enjoy it warm or room temperature.

w-vn-006.culturalNotes: Chè Trôi Nước is a traditional Vietnamese dessert usually served on special occasions and celebrations.

w-vn-007.title: Grass Jelly (Thạch Sương Sáo)

instructions.1: Transfer the grass jelly powder into a medium saucepan. Add the sugar and 2 cups of water. Stir together until the powder dissolves.
instructions.2: Add the remaining 2 cups of water and mix well.
instructions.3: Let the mixture rest for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Heat the mixture over medium heat. Use a spatula to stir the mixture, scraping the bottom of the pan where the powder settles.
instructions.5: After 3-4 minutes, the mixture will thicken and become lumpy. Use a whisk to quickly stir until the mixture is smooth. Continue stirring until the mixture comes to a gentle boil. Turn off the heat and continue stirring for 1 minute to ensure the mixture is smooth and free of lumps.
instructions.6: Transfer the grass jelly mixture to a heat-safe dish or bowl. Pop any bubbles with a toothpick or skim with a spoon.
instructions.7: Allow the mixture to cool at room temperature for 1-1.5 hours.
instructions.8: Transfer the dish to the refrigerator and chill for at least 2 hours.
instructions.9: To remove the jelly, invert the dish onto a large cutting board. Cut the grass jelly into cubes.
instructions.10: To serve, add some crushed ice to a dessert bowl. Add the grass jelly cubes. Sprinkle the jelly with a bit of sugar.
instructions.11: You can also use a wavy knife to cut the jelly into smaller pieces and add it to your favorite icy beverage.
instructions.12: Store any remaining grass jelly in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

w-vn-007.culturalNotes: Grass jelly is a traditional Vietnamese dessert, often served on hot days as a refreshing drink.

w-it-001.title: Cheese Agnolotti

instructions.1: Make a pile of flour on a work surface, and make a well in the center. Add eggs to the well, and scramble eggs with a fork, gradually incorporating flour from the edges. When the dough becomes too thick to use a fork, use a bench scraper to lift remaining dry flour over the top and begin to cut flour in until a shaggy dough forms.
instructions.2: Knead dough by hand until you have a smooth ball of dough, about 3 minutes. Cover and let rest for 10 to 15 minutes. Knead until a very smooth and elastic ball of dough forms, about 4 minutes more. Wrap tightly and rest dough in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours or up to overnight.
instructions.3: Add ricotta, Parmesan, egg yolk, parsley, salt, black pepper, and cayenne to a bowl, and stir together until evenly combined. Cover and refrigerate until needed.
instructions.4: Divide dough into 4 sections. Cover 3 sections with plastic, lightly flour a work surface, and shape the 4th into a rectangle. Use a rolling pin to roll dough into an 18x9-inch rectangle, thin enough to see your hand through.
instructions.5: Trim into 2 strips, approximately 18 by 4.5 inches. Maintain just enough flour on the work surface for this step and proceeding steps to prevent dough from sticking to the surface.
instructions.6: Transfer filling into a piping bag, or a plastic bag with 1 corner cut off, and pipe a 1/2-inch thick rope of filling lengthwise along each dough strip, 2 inches in from the edge. Mist each piece of dough very lightly with water.
instructions.7: Fold dough over filling, being careful not to trap any air bubbles. Press the 2 long edges of dough firmly together, flattening the seam to the thickness of a single layer of dough if possible. Use a fluted pasta cutter to trim excess dough to about 1/8-inch from the filling.
instructions.8: Starting at the end where the filling begins, and use two fingers to pinch the filling and dough together very tightly every inch to inch and a half. Bend the pressed sections of dough forward slightly. Use the pasta cutter to slice between each to form individual agnolotti. It may be helpful to mist the dough again before doing this step.
instructions.9: Transfer finished agnolotti to a lightly floured, parchment-lined pan. Cover and refrigerate until ready to cook. Agnolotti can also be frozen on the pan before being transferred into freezer bags for storage.
instructions.10: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook agnolotti for 3 minutes before transferring into the sauce of your choice.

w-it-001.culturalNotes: Agnolotti are stuffed, folded pasta and are a traditional dish from the Piedmont region of Italy.

w-it-002.title: Bruschetta

w-it-002-i1.name: Italian or French bread
w-it-002-i1.standardAmount: 1 loaf, sliced ½ inch (1.25 cm) thick on the bias

instructions.1: Toast the bread slices in a toaster oven, under a broiler, or on a grill until they turn golden.
instructions.2: Immediately rub the bread with the cut side of the garlic.
instructions.3: Sprinkle with salt and black pepper, and drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil.
instructions.4: Serve warm topped with whatever combinations of seasonal ingredients you choose.

w-it-002.culturalNotes: Bruschetta is a traditional Italian appetizer known for its simplicity and rich flavor.

w-it-003.title: Burrata with Marinated Fava Beans

instructions.1: Remove the fava beans from the pods and place them in a bowl.
instructions.2: Bring a pot of water to a boil and add the shelled fava beans. Boil for 4-5 minutes, then drain and rinse under cold water.
instructions.3: Pinch the outer skin of the fava beans on one end to tear it, gently squeeze and pop out the beans into a bowl, discarding the outer skins. Continue to remove the skins from all the fava beans in this manner.
instructions.4: Add the lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper to the fava beans and toss to mix.
instructions.5: Let the fava beans rest in the marinade for 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Slice the cheese and arrange it equally on four individual bowls.
instructions.7: Spoon the fava bean mixture on top, and then add two slices of grilled bread to each plate.
instructions.8: Enjoy!

w-it-003.culturalNotes: Burrata is a soft, creamy Italian cheese, often used in salads and appetizers.

w-it-004.title: Sausage and Eggplant Calzone

instructions.1: Preheat your oven to its highest temperature.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and onions until translucent.
instructions.3: Add the eggplant and crumbled halal beef sausage and cook until both are golden.
instructions.4: Add the tomato sauce, a pinch of red pepper flakes, salt and pepper, and chopped basil and cook on low for 20 minutes until very thick.
instructions.5: Mix together the ricotta cheese, mozzarella cheese, and parmesan cheese and set aside.
instructions.6: Prepare your pizza dough, and after the first rising by rolling it into a 12-inch circle and laying it across a pan prepared by lightly oiling or sprinkling with cornmeal.
instructions.7: Spoon the halal beef sausage and eggplant mixture on one half of the calzone, keeping a 1-inch border clean.
instructions.8: Add the cheese mixture and spread over the eggplant.
instructions.9: Fold the top half of the dough across, and pinch the edges to seal.
instructions.10: Bake for about 10 minutes or until puffy and golden.

w-it-004.culturalNotes: Calzone is a popular dish in Italy, especially in the south. It is served as a snack or main meal.

w-it-005.title: Cassata Siciliana

instructions.1: Soak the raisins in orange juice for 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Mix the ricotta cheese with powdered sugar, cinnamon, and cocoa powder.
instructions.3: Add the soaked raisins and crushed cookies to the ricotta mixture.
instructions.4: Place the ricotta mixture in a greased round mold.
instructions.5: Boil the heavy cream and chocolate in a small saucepan until the chocolate melts and the mixture is smooth.
instructions.6: Pour the chocolate mixture over the cassata and let it cool in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
instructions.7: Cut the cassata into slices and serve.

w-it-005.culturalNotes: Cassata Siciliana is a traditional dessert from the island of Sicily, Italy, known for its rich and sweet flavor.

w-it-006.title: Pizza With Cherry Tomatoes And Goat Cheese

w-it-006-i4.name: Sea Salt And Cracked Black Pepper

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to its highest setting.
instructions.2: Mix together the tomatoes, garlic, olive oil, salt, pepper, and chopped fresh basil in a bowl. Stir well and set aside.
instructions.3: With your hands, stretch the pizza dough onto a 12-inch circle and place it on a pizza peel sprinkled with cornmeal to prevent sticking.
instructions.4: Mix together 2 tablespoons of olive oil and pesto and brush this mixture onto the pizza dough, leaving a 1-inch border.
instructions.5: Scatter the mozzarella slices evenly across the dough, then the tomatoes.
instructions.6: Crumble the goat cheese over the pizza.
instructions.7: Bake for 12-15 minutes or until the pizza crust is lightly browned and the cheese is bubbly.

w-it-006.culturalNotes: This pizza is a popular dish in Italian cuisine, known for its simplicity and rich flavor.

w-it-007.title: Ciabatta Bread

instructions.1: For the biga, sprinkle the yeast over the water in a large bowl, and let sit 5 to 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the flours, and stir to combine (the dough may seem stiff, but will soften up as it sits).
instructions.3: Cover the biga tightly with plastic wrap, and let it sit for 6 hours at room temperature.
instructions.4: Stir it, and refrigerate it until the next day, or at least 12 hours.
instructions.5: Combine the flour, salt, and yeast in a large bowl, then add the water and biga, and stir until the dough is mixed (the dough will be quite wet and rough in texture).
instructions.6: Turn the dough out onto a floured counter or breadboard, and using as little flour as possible, knead for 5 minutes, or until the dough is smooth (don't worry that your dough still seems very loose and moist, as it will firm up as it rises).
instructions.7: Place the dough into a large bowl three times the size of the dough that has been lightly oiled first.
instructions.8: Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and let sit in a warm spot for 2 to 3 hours, or until the dough has doubled, punching down and turning the dough every 30 minutes or so.
instructions.9: If using baking sheets, sprinkle them lightly with cornmeal.
instructions.10: Divide the dough in two pieces and fold each into a rectangle.
instructions.11: Stretch the rectangle until it is about 12 to 14 inches long.
instructions.12: Place each prepared loaf onto a baking sheet, and cover lightly with a towel.
instructions.13: If you are using a baking stone, flour two kitchen towels, or bread making peels with flour, and place the shaped loaves on them to rise.
instructions.15: Preheat the oven at this time to 450 degrees F.
instructions.16: After 45 minutes, place the baking sheets into the hot oven, or move the loaves onto the hot baking stone.
instructions.17: Bake for about 30 minutes, rotating the loaves once during this time, or until the dough is a dark golden brown all over.
instructions.18: Remove and let cool on a wire rack.

w-it-007.culturalNotes: Ciabatta is a traditional Italian bread known for its thin, flat shape and distinctive texture. It is often served with various Italian dishes.

w-it-008.title: Colomba Pasquale

w-it-008-i8.name: orange zest and vanilla seeds
w-it-008-i8.standardAmount: 1/2 teaspoon (or seeds of 1 vanilla pod and zest of 1 orange)

instructions.1: The night before, mix the big ingredients in a small bowl, cover, and let rise overnight.
instructions.2: The next day, in a large bowl, add the big starter, the flour, salt, yeast, sugar, butter, eggs, and the orange zest and vanilla seeds.
instructions.3: Use a wooden spoon to mix into a shaggy dough, then add the candied orange and raisins.
instructions.4: Dump the dough out onto a lightly floured counter, and knead by hand until the dough is very smooth and elastic, about 7 to 8 minutes.
instructions.5: Alternately, mix ingredients in a stand mixer with a dough hook until smooth.
instructions.6: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap and place in a warm spot in your kitchen to rise for 2 to 3 hours until soft and almost doubled in size.
instructions.7: Divide the dough into two pieces and either place in your Colomba form, or shape by hand by forming a cross shape.
instructions.8: Place the dough on a parchment lined baking sheet, cover with greased plastic wrap and let rise again for another 2 hours.
instructions.9: At the end of your rising time, preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
instructions.10: Make your topping by beating the egg whites until foamy, then adding the almond flour, and sugar.
instructions.11: Liberally brush the top and sides of the bread with the egg white mixture and then scatter the pearl sugar and sliced almonds on top.
instructions.12: Bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until a cake tester comes out cleanly when inserted in the center. (If the bread darkens too much when baking, tent some aluminum foil on top.)
instructions.13: Cool completely, slice, and enjoy!

w-it-008.culturalNotes: Colomba Pasquale is a traditional Italian Easter bread, typically enjoyed during the Easter holiday.

w-it-009.title: Palermo Style Chicken Cutlets With Pistachio Caper Sauce

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
instructions.2: Cut the chicken breasts into three pieces lengthways, then pound with a mallet until equal thickness.
instructions.3: Place the seasoned flour in a plastic bag, and one by one drop in each chicken cutlet, tossing to coat.
instructions.4: Place the eggs and milk in one bowl and beat until blended.
instructions.5: Place the breading ingredients in another bowl, and stir to combine.
instructions.6: Line a 13 x 9 inch sided baking sheet with foil, and coat with the oil and butter for baking.
instructions.7: Dip each floured cutlet, first in the egg mixture, then in the crumb mixture.
instructions.8: Line the breaded cutlets side by side in the prepared pan, then bake for 10 minutes.
instructions.9: Turn the cutlets over, and bake another 8 minutes or until golden and cooked through.
instructions.10: While the cutlets are baking, place the sauce ingredients into a small blender and pulse until finely chopped, but not smooth.
instructions.11: Arrange the cooked cutlets onto a platter, then spoon some of the sauce on top.
instructions.12: Serve, offering additional sauce at the table.

w-it-009.culturalNotes: Cotoletta is a famous dish in Sicily, especially in Palermo, where it is served with a pistachio and caper sauce.

w-it-010.title: Fettuccine Alfredo

instructions.1: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the pasta.
instructions.2: Remove 1/4 cup of the cream to a separate bowl and whisk the egg yolk into it.
instructions.3: In a saucepan, heat the remaining cream and chicken broth.
instructions.4: Cook the pasta al dente, then drain the pasta and return it to the pot.
instructions.5: Stir the butter into the pasta until melted and the butter covers each strand of pasta.
instructions.6: Whisk a little of the hot cream mixture into the egg and cream mixture and stir. (This warms the egg mixture without cooking it completely.)
instructions.7: Next, add the remaining hot cream and broth into the egg mixture and mix well.
instructions.8: Finally, pour the combined egg and cream mixture over the pasta and toss to coat evenly.
instructions.9: Add the grated cheese, and a dash of sea salt to taste.
instructions.10: Divide the pasta into 4 separate dishes and top with cracked black pepper and offer additional cheese.

w-it-010.culturalNotes: Fettuccine Alfredo is a traditional Italian dish known for its rich cream and cheese sauce.

w-it-011.title: Fennel Parmesan (Finocchi alla Parmigiana)

instructions.1: Cut off the tops of the fennel bulbs, then cut them in half. Use a sharp knife to cut out the core section, then cut into slices lengthwise about 1/3 inch thick.
instructions.2: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil, and then add the fennel and cook just until fork tender, about 4 to 5 minutes. Drain the fennel and set aside.
instructions.3: Add the oil to a pot over medium heat and once lightly smoking add the onions. Cook the onions, stirring often, until tender, about 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the garlic, and cook just until fragrant, an additional minute or two.
instructions.5: Add the tomatoes, oregano, red pepper flakes (if using), parsley, basil, salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook until thickened, about 15 to 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F.
instructions.7: In a large 13 x 9 oven-proof casserole dish, spread half the fennel over the bottom. Spoon enough sauce just to cover, then scatter half the diced mozzarella and grated cheese on top.
instructions.8: Add the rest of the fennel, then cover with the sauce and remaining cheese.
instructions.9: Bake the casserole for 35 to 40 minutes or until it is bubbly and golden on top.
instructions.10: Let rest 10 minutes, then serve.

w-it-011.culturalNotes: Fennel Parmesan (Finocchi alla Parmigiana) is a traditional Italian dish that combines the flavor of fennel with Parmesan cheese.

w-it-012.title: Focaccia

instructions.1: Sprinkle one teaspoon of the yeast over ½ cup of the water in a medium bowl. Stir to mix, and let stand 10 minutes. Add ¾ cup flour, cover tightly with plastic and let rise in warm place until doubled, about 45 minutes.
instructions.2: In a large bowl, sprinkle the remaining teaspoon of yeast over 1 cup of warm water, mix and let stand 10 minutes. Add the first yeast mixture (now risen) along with 3 tablespoons of olive oil and 2 teaspoons of salt, mix well. Add the remaining flour gradually, mixing well after each addition until well incorporated.
instructions.3: On a lightly floured work surface, turn the dough out and knead until soft, about 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover tightly and let rise in warm place until doubled, about 1 ½ hours.
instructions.5: Oil an 11" x 14" (28 cm x 36 cm) baking pan and turn the risen dough out onto the pan, flattening it out to the edges. If the dough springs back too much to cover the pan, allow it to rest for 10 minutes before resuming. Cover with a clean towel and let rise 45 minutes to an hour.
instructions.6: Preheat oven to 425 °F (220 °C). Remove towel and press indentations into the dough with your fingertips, then drizzle with the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil, sprinkle with sea salt and place pan in oven. Bake 20 to 25 minutes, or until the top is golden.
instructions.7: Remove the focaccia from the pan as soon as it is out of the oven and let cool on a rack before serving.

w-it-012.culturalNotes: Focaccia is a traditional Italian flatbread, often served as a snack or part of a lunch.

w-it-013.title: Sweet Potato Frittata

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
instructions.2: In an oven-safe skillet, sauté the onion in vegetable oil until soft.
instructions.3: Add the diced sweet potatoes and cook until tender, stirring occasionally.
instructions.4: In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, salt, and pepper.
instructions.5: Pour the egg mixture over the sweet potato mixture in the skillet.
instructions.6: Let the mixture set on the sides, then place the skillet in the preheated oven.
instructions.7: Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until completely set.
instructions.8: Slice the frittata and serve hot.

w-it-013.culturalNotes: Frittata is a traditional Italian dish made with eggs and vegetables. It can be served as a main course or as an appetizer.

w-it-014.title: Vanilla Gelato Italiano

instructions.1: In a large bowl, beat the egg yolks and sugar until the mixture is light and thick.
instructions.2: In a heavy saucepan, heat the milk, cream, vanilla pod, and salt over medium heat until bubbles begin to form around the edges.
instructions.3: Remove the saucepan from the heat, and take 1/2 cup of the hot milk mixture, and slowly whisk it into the beaten eggs.
instructions.4: Next, whisk the egg mixture into the saucepan, and cook over low heat, stirring continuously until the mixture thickens, about 8 to 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve into a metal bowl and refrigerate until cold.
instructions.6: Once the custard mixture is cold, transfer it into an ice cream maker and churn following the manufacturer's instructions.
instructions.7: Serve the gelato immediately, or freeze in an airtight container until you are ready to use.

w-it-014.culturalNotes: Italian gelato is a traditional frozen dessert in Italy, known for its creamy texture and rich flavor.

w-it-015.title: Gnocchi Caprese

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F.
instructions.2: Wash and dry the potatoes, then bake them until they are fork-tender, about 45 minutes.
instructions.3: While the potatoes are baking, prepare the tomato sauce: Heat the oil in a heavy saucepan over medium heat, and add the garlic.
instructions.4: As soon as the garlic begins to sizzle, add the tomatoes and turn the heat to high. Once the sauce begins to bubble, turn the heat back down to medium-low.
instructions.5: Season with salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using), and add the basil. Cook for another minute or two and remove from the heat.
instructions.6: Remove the potatoes from the oven and scoop out the pulp from the skins, then press it through a potato ricer.
instructions.7: While still warm, place the riced potatoes on a large board forming a mound with a hole in the center. Add the yolk and the salt into the center.
instructions.8: Slowly start adding the flour a little at a time, mixing well with your hands until you have created a soft, workable dough.
instructions.9: Knead gently only briefly until you have achieved a smooth, pliable if slightly sticky dough.
instructions.10: To shape the gnocchi, first break the dough into fist-sized pieces, and roll each piece into a log about the thickness of your thumb.
instructions.11: Cut into 1-inch pieces.
instructions.12: To finish, take a fork and place it against your work board. With its back towards you, press each piece of dough with your index finger firmly up the length of the fork tines.
instructions.13: Let the gnocchi fall back onto the board and continue with the remaining pieces in this manner.
instructions.14: Place the prepared gnocchi on a lightly floured baking sheet and either cook immediately, or keep refrigerated until ready to use, preferably not more than 3 hours.
instructions.15: To cook, drop carefully into salted boiling water and remove immediately as they have all floated to the surface.
instructions.16: Drain the gnocchi and top with the hot sauce.
instructions.17: Add the chunks of cheese along with the chopped basil, and stir carefully so the cheese begins to soften and melt.

w-it-015.culturalNotes: Gnocchi Caprese is a traditional Italian dish combining potato gnocchi with tomato sauce and fresh mozzarella cheese.

w-it-016.title: Gnudi with Quick Tomato Sauce

w-it-016-i2.name: 1 (28 Ounce) Can Imported Diced Italian Tomatoes

instructions.1: Cook the spinach by steaming or in the microwave. Drain and squeeze out all excess water.
instructions.2: Chop finely, and then drain once more.
instructions.3: Place the spinach, ricotta, eggs, parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and flour into a mixing bowl, and mix together well.
instructions.4: Place a cup and a half of semolina flour on a baking sheet.
instructions.5: Form the dumplings by using floured hands, lightly rolling the gnocchi to coat in the semolina flour.
instructions.6: Place the dumplings in the refrigerator overnight on an uncovered tray.
instructions.7: To make the sauce, heat the oil in a heavy saucepan over medium heat, and add the garlic.
instructions.8: As soon as the garlic begins to sizzle, but before it takes on color, add the tomatoes.
instructions.9: Turn the heat to high, and as soon as the sauce begins to bubble, turn back down to medium low.
instructions.10: Season with salt and pepper, and red pepper flakes if you are using them, and add the basil. Cook for another minute or two and keep warm.
instructions.11: Bring to boil a large pot of salted water.
instructions.12: Drop dumplings into boiling water, then lower to a simmer.
instructions.13: When the dumplings float to the top, they are done. Remove with a slotted spoon or ladle and return to the pot.
instructions.14: Toss gently with the tomato sauce, and serve with parmesan cheese.

w-it-016.culturalNotes: Gnudi are small ricotta and spinach dumplings, a traditional dish from Tuscany, Italy.

w-it-017.title: Malloreddus (Sardinian Gnocchi) in Lamb Broth

instructions.1: Start the lamb broth: Place the lamb neck bones in a large pot and add enough water to cover the bones. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for an hour.
instructions.2: Add the carrots, celery, onion, potatoes, parsley, rosemary, and sun-dried tomatoes. Simmer for another 30 minutes.
instructions.3: In a large bowl, mix the semolina flour with the warm water and salt. Knead the ingredients until the dough is smooth and pliable.
instructions.4: Spread the dough on a floured surface and cut it into small pieces. Shape the pieces into small, round gnocchi.
instructions.5: Add the malloreddus to the simmering broth and cook for 10 minutes until tender.
instructions.6: Serve the malloreddus in bowls and sprinkle with grated cheese.

w-it-017.culturalNotes: Malloreddus is a traditional type of gnocchi from Sardinia, Italy, and is typically served in a lamb broth or with sauces.

w-it-018.title: Stamped Marzipan Cookies With Dark Chocolate

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
instructions.2: In a small bowl, stir together the flour and salt.
instructions.3: In a second bowl, using an electric hand mixer, beat together the butter, sugar, and grated marzipan until blended.
instructions.4: Add the finely ground almonds and egg yolk and blend well.
instructions.5: Dump the flour into the butter mixture and blend on low speed just until mixed.
instructions.6: Empty the bowl onto a lightly floured counter and gently knead with your hands for a minute or two until you have a smooth ball.
instructions.7: Divide the dough in half, and roll out about 1/3 inch thick and use a cookie stamp or cutter and cut out the cookies.
instructions.8: Place the cookies onto the prepared baking sheets and roll out the rest of the dough in the same manner.
instructions.9: Bake the cookies for 18 to 20 minutes or just until they begin to brown at the edges (do not let the cookies brown!).
instructions.10: Remove the cookies from the oven and cool completely.
instructions.11: If using a cookie stamp, fill with melted chocolate or jam and let sit until set.
instructions.12: Store cookies in an airtight container and enjoy!

w-it-018.culturalNotes: Stamped Marzipan Cookies with Dark Chocolate are a traditional Italian sweet served on special occasions.

w-it-019.title: Summer Milanese Minestrone

instructions.1: Heat the olive oil in a large stockpot, then add the onions, carrots, celery, and zucchini and cook for 3 to 4 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the green beans and potatoes and cook for an additional 3 minutes.
instructions.3: Add the tomatoes and 6 cups of the broth (the vegetables should be covered with the broth coming about one inch above the vegetables in the pot).
instructions.4: Season lightly with salt and pepper, cover, and reduce the heat to a simmer.
instructions.5: Cook for about 2 hours, adding additional broth if needed.
instructions.6: Add the spinach and rice and cook for another 20 to 30 minutes or until the rice is just about tender to the bite.
instructions.7: The soup should be thickened, not too thin or watery, and the vegetables meltingly tender.
instructions.8: Stir in the chopped basil, adjust the seasoning and allow to come to room temperature.
instructions.9: Serve in individual bowls with a drizzle of olive oil, cracked black pepper, and grated cheese if desired.

w-it-019.culturalNotes: Minestrone is a traditional Italian soup known for its variety of vegetable and grain ingredients. This dish is particularly popular in Milan during the summer.

w-it-020.title: Neapolitan-Style Pizza Dough with Garlic and Italian Seasonings

instructions.1: In a large bowl, mix flour, salt, and yeast until thoroughly combined.
instructions.2: Add ice water, mixing well until a soft dough forms. Add 2 tablespoons of olive oil and mix.
instructions.3: Turn the dough out onto a floured work surface and knead until the dough is firm but slightly sticky, adding more flour if needed. Knead in the granulated garlic and Italian seasoning.
instructions.4: Shape the dough into a ball and place it in an oiled bowl. Brush the top with 0.5 teaspoon of olive oil, cover the bowl with plastic wrap, and let the dough rise until doubled, 1 to 2 hours.
instructions.5: Punch down the dough and cut it in half. Shape each half into a 12-inch pizza crust and place on pizza pans.
instructions.6: Move a rack to the bottom position in the oven and preheat the oven to 230 degrees Celsius (450 degrees Fahrenheit).
instructions.7: Bake the pizza crusts on the bottom rack until firm, 3 to 7 minutes. Allow the crusts to cool for about 10 minutes before topping with sauce, cheese, or other desired ingredients and returning to the oven to bake.

w-it-020.culturalNotes: Neapolitan pizza is a traditional dish from Naples, Italy, known for its thin crust and puffy edges.

w-it-021.title: Cocoa Panforte

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 150 degrees C (300 degrees F). Line an 8- or 9-inch baking pan with a removable bottom with rice paper or parchment paper, including the sides.
instructions.2: Combine honey and sugar in a small pan over low heat and stir until sugar is dissolved, about 3 minutes. Bring to a gentle boil, and do not stir once syrup begins to boil. Heat to 115 degrees C (240 degrees F) or until a small amount of syrup dropped into cold water forms a soft ball that flattens when removed from water and placed on a flat surface. Remove from heat and stir in pine nuts, walnuts, almonds, pineapple, ginger, dates, cocoa powder, coriander, allspice, and nutmeg. The mixture will be very stiff.
instructions.3: Press the mixture into the prepared baking pan.
instructions.4: Bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes. Remove from oven and place the pan on a cooling rack to cool completely.
instructions.5: Remove the panforte from the baking pan and dust with confectioners' sugar.

w-it-021.culturalNotes: Panforte is a traditional Italian sweet from the city of Siena, known for its rich combination of dried fruits and nuts.

w-it-022.title: Panini (Italian Sandwich)

instructions.1: For the biga, sprinkle the yeast over the water in a large bowl large enough to fit all of the ingredients, and let sit 5 to 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Add the flours, and stir to combine. (The dough may seem stiff, but will soften up as it sits.)
instructions.3: Cover the biga tightly with plastic wrap, and let it sit for 6 hours at room temperature.
instructions.4: Stir the biga, and refrigerate it until the next day, or at least 12 hours.
instructions.5: For the buns, combine the flour, salt, and yeast in a large bowl.
instructions.6: Add the water and biga, and stir until the dough is mixed. (It will be quite wet, and rough in texture.)
instructions.7: Turn the dough out onto a floured counter or breadboard, and using as little flour as possible, knead for 5 minutes, or until the dough is smooth. (Don't worry that your dough still seems very loose and moist, as it will firm up as it rises.)
instructions.8: Place the dough into a large bowl three times the size of the dough that has been lightly oiled first.
instructions.9: Cover tightly with plastic wrap, and let sit in a warm spot for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until the dough has doubled, punching down and turning the dough every 30 minutes or so.
instructions.10: If using baking sheets, sprinkle them lightly with cornmeal.
instructions.11: Divide the dough into balls about 3 inches in diameter.
instructions.12: Work with your hands until they are evenly shaped.
instructions.13: Lightly roll in extra flour and place on your prepared baking sheet or bread peel.
instructions.14: Lightly press each ball with the heel of your hand to create a disc shape.
instructions.16: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F.
instructions.17: Fill a shallow casserole dish with water and place in the oven 10 minutes before you place the buns into the oven.
instructions.18: After 45 minutes, place the baking sheets into the hot oven, or move the buns with the peel onto the hot baking stone.
instructions.19: Bake for about 20 minutes, rotating the buns once during this time, or until the dough is a light golden brown all over.
instructions.20: Remove and let cool on a wire rack.

w-it-022.culturalNotes: Panini is a type of small Italian bread, commonly used for making sandwiches.

w-it-023.title: Panzerotti

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a small saucepan, then cook the garlic for a minute or two until fragrant.
instructions.2: Add the tomatoes, oregano, salt, and pepper and cook until you have a thick sauce, about 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Take the dough after the first rising, and shape it into a long loaf, then divide it into 10 pieces and shape into balls.
instructions.4: Roll each ball on a lightly floured surface into a 4-inch diameter circle.
instructions.5: Place a spoonful of tomato mixture on each circle, sprinkle with fresh basil, salt, and pepper, and cover with some of the mozzarella.
instructions.6: Lightly moisten the edges with water and pinch to seal.
instructions.7: Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed pan to 375 degrees F.
instructions.8: Fry in batches until golden brown, then drain well on paper towels and serve hot.

w-it-023.culturalNotes: Panzerotti are a popular dish in southern Italy, especially in the Puglia region. They are typically served as a snack or main course.

w-it-024.title: Pappa al Pomodoro

instructions.1: In a large pot, sauté the onions in the oil over medium heat until they are translucent.
instructions.2: Add the garlic and cook until fragrant.
instructions.3: Add the tomatoes and bring to a boil.
instructions.4: Reduce the soup to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes to thicken the tomatoes.
instructions.5: Add the broth and mix well, then cook for another 10 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the bread cubes and basil, and then season with salt and pepper.
instructions.7: Simmer for an additional 10 minutes.
instructions.8: Use a whisk to break up the bread and thicken the soup.
instructions.9: Remove from the heat and cool to room temperature.
instructions.10: Serve the soup in individual bowls topped with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkling of cracked black pepper.

w-it-024.culturalNotes: Pappa al Pomodoro is a traditional Italian soup from Tuscany, known for its simplicity and rich flavor.

w-it-025.title: Pasta allo scarpariello

instructions.1: Put a pot of water on to boil for the pasta. Add salt once the water starts to boil and bring to the boil again.
instructions.2: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and add the crushed garlic until it starts to soften. Then add the peperoncino (if using) and some of the basil.
instructions.3: Add the datterini or cherry tomatoes cut into halves or quarters (or canned peeled tomatoes). When the tomatoes have softened, pour in the tomato passata.
instructions.4: Simmer for about 15 minutes, remove the garlic and add salt and pepper to taste.
instructions.5: Cook the pasta a couple of minutes less than necessary for it to be al dente (it will finish cooking in the tomato sauce), drain it and add to the sauce. Cook both together for 2-3 more minutes until the pasta is cooked.
instructions.6: Turn the heat to low and add the Parmigiano and pecorino cheese a handful at a time while mixing everything together well. You want the cheese to melt in the hot sauce.
instructions.7: Serve immediately with fresh basil leaves and extra cheese if required.

w-it-025.culturalNotes: Pasta allo scarpariello is a traditional dish from southern Italy, known for its rich tomato and chili sauce.

w-it-026.title: Pasta and Bean Soup (Pasta e Fagioli)

w-it-026-i5.name: crushed or ground hot red pepper

instructions.1: Wash the dried white beans and soak them in salted water (3 parts water to 1 part beans) for 12 hours or bring to a boil for 2 minutes and let stand, covered, for 1 hour.
instructions.2: Do not drain the beans, but bring them to a boil. Skim off the foam and add the olive oil, garlic, and bay leaf.
instructions.3: Simmer the beans for about 2 hours, or until tender.
instructions.4: Cook the macaroni for 6-7 minutes, but don't let it get too soft.
instructions.5: Drain the pasta and save some of the cooking water.
instructions.6: Stir the pasta and red pepper into the beans and simmer until the pasta is al dente, adding some of the saved water if necessary.
instructions.7: Garnish with red pepper to taste and fresh parsley.

w-it-026.culturalNotes: Pasta e Fagioli is a traditional Italian dish that combines pasta and beans in a warm, nourishing soup.

w-es-001.title: Arroz Negro (Arròs Negre)

instructions.1: Add 3 cups of fish broth to a saucepan and a pinch of saffron threads and heat on medium heat.
instructions.2: Finely chop 1/2 onion, roughly chop 4 cloves of garlic, finely chop 1/2 Italian sweet green pepper, finely grate 2 tomatoes, and cut one cleaned cuttlefish (tentacles removed) into medium-sized cubes.
instructions.3: Heat a paella pan on medium heat and add 1/4 cup of extra virgin olive oil.
instructions.4: After 1 minute, season the olive oil with sea salt and add the pieces of cuttlefish, mix with the olive oil. After 2 minutes and the cuttlefish is lightly sautéed, remove from the pan and set aside.
instructions.5: Using the same pan and the same heat, add the chopped onion and Italian sweet pepper, mix with the olive oil. After 3 minutes and the onion is translucent, add the chopped garlic and continue to mix. After 30 seconds, add 1/2 tsp of sweet smoked Spanish paprika, quickly mix together, then add the finely grated tomato (about 1/2 cup - 115 grams), mix together and simmer.
instructions.6: After 3 minutes and the tomato sauce has thickened, add 1 cup of uncooked Spanish round rice, 1/4 oz of squid ink, and season everything with sea salt and black pepper, mix continuously for about 2 minutes, then pour in the saffron-infused fish broth and the cuttlefish we cooked earlier, give it one final mix so everything is evenly distributed, do not mix again.
instructions.7: About 8 to 9 minutes after turning up the heat, and a lot of the broth has been absorbed by the rice, but there is still some left, lower the fire to a low-medium heat, simmer for 3 to 5 minutes or until all the broth has been absorbed, then turn the heat back up to medium-high and go for 90 seconds to achieve the socarrat, then remove the pan from the heat, cover with a dishcloth and let it sit for 5 minutes.
instructions.8: Uncover the pan and garnish with lemon wedges and sprinkle with finely chopped fresh parsley, enjoy!

w-es-001.culturalNotes: Arroz Negro (Arròs Negre) is a traditional dish from Spain, particularly from the Valencia region. It is known for its deep black color and rich cuttlefish flavor.

w-es-002.title: Arroz a la Cubana

instructions.1: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the potato and carrot and sauté for 3 minutes. Remove to a bowl.
instructions.2: Add the onion and garlic to the hot skillet and sauté until slightly brown, 5-7 minutes. Add the ground beef and cook, stirring until browned and crumbly, 5-7 minutes.
instructions.3: Return the potato-carrot mixture to the skillet with the water, soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender, 5-8 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the bell pepper, raisins, and peas and cook until heated through, about 2 minutes. Serve over hot cooked rice.

w-es-002.culturalNotes: Arroz a la Cubana is a popular dish in Spain, featuring a mix of ground beef, vegetables, and spices, served over rice.

w-es-003.title: Basque Garlic Soup (Zurrukutuna)

instructions.1: Cut the baguette into slices that are 1.25 cm thick, then place them on a baking tray lined with foil, and bake in a preheated oven at 200°C / 400°F for 10 minutes or until the slices are lightly toasted, then set aside.
instructions.2: Heat a stockpot over medium heat and add the olive oil.
instructions.3: After a couple of minutes, add the sliced garlic and crushed red pepper, and mix continuously for 1 minute, then add the toasted baguette slices and continue to mix for 3 minutes, then add the sweet smoked Spanish paprika and quickly mix together, then add the grated tomatoes and season with salt and pepper, and continue to mix together.
instructions.4: About 3 minutes after adding the grated tomatoes, add the vegetable broth and bay leaf, raise to a high heat, and mix, once it comes to a boil, place a lid on the pan and lower to a low heat, mix every 2-3 minutes to help break the pieces of bread apart.
instructions.5: While the soup is simmering, place the cod fillet on some paper towels and pat dry, then season with salt and pepper and finely chop, crack the eggs into a bowl, season with salt, and whisk together.
instructions.6: After simmering the soup for 15 minutes and the pieces of bread are broken apart, remove the bay leaf, add the chopped cod and mix into the soup, simmer for 3 minutes, then slowly add the whisked eggs while gently mixing together, then place a lid on the pan and turn off the heat.
instructions.7: After a couple of minutes, remove the lid and transfer the soup into shallow bowls, garnish with chopped parsley, and enjoy!

w-es-003.culturalNotes: Basque Garlic Soup (Zurrukutuna) is a traditional dish from the Basque Country in Spain, known for its rich flavor and strong flavors.

w-es-004.title: Boquerones en Vinagre

instructions.1: Start by cleaning the sardines. Remove the head, viscera, and spine using your thumb. Then rinse the sardines under cold water and place them in a bowl, adding a bit of sea salt.
instructions.2: Lay the sardines flat in a glass baking dish. It is important to use a glass dish and not metal to avoid giving the fish a metallic taste.
instructions.3: Cover the sardines with lemon juice and vinegar. Tip: Add more vinegar than lemon juice, as the lemon flavor will become bitter the next day.
instructions.4: Chop the parsley finely and sprinkle it over the sardines.
instructions.5: Add a second layer of sardines and repeat the process.
instructions.6: Cover the glass dish with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
instructions.7: Before serving, rinse the sardines with cold water, then garnish with chopped parsley and a bit of sea salt. Serve with rustic bread.

w-es-004.culturalNotes: Boquerones en Vinagre is a traditional tapas dish in Spain, often served as an appetizer in bars and cafes.

w-es-005.title: Crema Catalana

instructions.1: Add 2 cups of organic milk to a saucepan along with 8 lemon peels, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 split vanilla bean, and 2 tablespoons of sugar. Bring the mixture to a light boil over medium heat, then turn off the heat and let the milk infuse for 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Separate the yolks from the whites of 5 large organic eggs (discard the whites). Add 2 tablespoons of sugar to the yolks and whisk together. In a separate bowl, mix 1/2 cup of cold organic milk with 1 tablespoon of cornstarch and whisk until smooth. Add the cold milk mixture to the yolks and whisk until well combined.
instructions.3: Strain the infused milk into the egg mixture and whisk until well incorporated. Return the mixture to the saucepan and heat over medium heat, whisking continuously for 9-10 minutes until it thickens. Turn off the heat and continue whisking for another 30 seconds.
instructions.4: Transfer the mixture to 4 individual ramekins. After 20 minutes, cover them with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
instructions.5: Before serving, sprinkle 1 tablespoon of sugar on top of each ramekin and use a kitchen torch to caramelize the sugar until it turns a deep golden color.

w-es-005.culturalNotes: Crema Catalana is a traditional dessert from Catalonia, Spain, known for its rich flavor and crispy caramelized top.

w-es-006.title: Fabada Asturiana

instructions.1: Drain the white beans into a sieve and rinse them under cold running water.
instructions.2: Peel 3 cloves of garlic and finely mince them, finely dice half an onion, and cut the sausages into 1-inch thick pieces.
instructions.3: Heat a large saucepan over medium heat and add a generous tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil. After 2 minutes, add the sausages and stir for 4 minutes until they are browned, then remove them from the pan and set aside.
instructions.4: In the same pan, add the diced onions and minced garlic, and stir for 3 minutes until the onions are translucent. Add 1 teaspoon of sweet smoked Spanish paprika and stir quickly.
instructions.5: Return the sausages to the pan, add the drained white beans, and stir well to combine. Add 1.5 cups of cold water, a pinch of sea salt, and 1/2 teaspoon of saffron threads, and stir gently.
instructions.6: Cover the pan and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes. Remove the lid and turn off the heat; the water should have thickened into a rich broth.
instructions.7: Transfer the fabada to shallow bowls and serve hot.

w-es-006.culturalNotes: Fabada Asturiana is a traditional dish from the Asturias region in northern Spain, known for its rich flavor and distinctive spices.

w-es-007.title: Spanish Fish & Tomato Stew

instructions.1: Heat a large pot over medium heat and add the olive oil.
instructions.2: After a couple of minutes, add the chopped onion, garlic, celery, and carrot, and stir continuously for 5 minutes until the vegetables are lightly sautéed.
instructions.3: Add the sweet smoked Spanish paprika and dried thyme, and quickly mix together, then add the diced tomatoes, fish broth, saffron, and season with salt and pepper, then raise the heat to high and give it a gentle mix.
instructions.4: In the meantime, cut the baby potatoes in half, and if you are using larger potatoes, cut them into 2 cm thick bite-sized pieces.
instructions.5: Once the broth comes to a boil, add the chopped potatoes, mix together, then place a lid on the pot and lower the heat to low-medium.
instructions.6: While the stew is simmering, place the cod fillets on paper towels and pat dry, season with salt and pepper, and then cut each fillet into 2 evenly sized pieces for a total of 6 pieces of fish.
instructions.7: After simmering the potatoes for 20 minutes and they are cooked through, add the cod fillets over the stew, all in a single layer, then gently flip each one so they're fully coated in the broth, then place the lid back on the pot and simmer for 5 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.
instructions.8: Serve the stew directly from the pot or transfer it to shallow bowls, topped with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice and some chopped parsley.

w-es-007.culturalNotes: This Spanish fish and tomato stew is a traditional dish in Spanish cuisine, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-es-008.title: French Fries

instructions.1: Cut the edges of the potatoes to make a rectangle. Slice into 1/2-inch slabs. Cut each slab into several sticks.
instructions.2: Immerse the sticks in cold water for at least 30 minutes (you can also store them in the fridge overnight this way). Alternatively, rinse the potatoes under cold water until the water runs clear. The goal is to get rid of all the loose starch that will make the fries stick to each other.
instructions.3: Carefully dry the potatoes with towels right before frying.
instructions.4: Preheat the oil to 320°F. Fry the sticks in small batches (about a handful at a time) for about 5 minutes, or until cooked through but not brown. Be sure to let the oil heat up between batches. Drain the sticks over a cookie sheet.
instructions.5: Let the sticks sit for about 30 minutes.
instructions.6: Heat the oil to 375°F. Fry the sticks until light brown and crispy, about 2-4 minutes. Drain the sticks over a cookie sheet.
instructions.7: Sprinkle with salt and serve immediately.

w-es-008.culturalNotes: French fries are a popular dish in Spain, known as 'French fries' or 'papas fritas'.

w-es-009.title: Croquetas de Pavo (Turkey Croquettes)

instructions.1: Heat 4 tablespoons (about 60 grams) of unsalted butter and 60 ml of extra virgin olive oil in a pan over low heat until the butter melts.
instructions.2: Add finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-6 minutes until it turns golden.
instructions.3: Add a pinch of salt and nutmeg and stir well.
instructions.4: Add finely chopped halal turkey ham and stir for one minute.
instructions.5: Add the flour and stir the mixture constantly for one minute.
instructions.6: Gradually add the milk while stirring continuously for 15-20 minutes until the mixture thickens and becomes creamy.
instructions.7: Pour the mixture into a large bowl and let it cool to room temperature, then cover it with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
instructions.8: Shape the cold mixture into small croquettes and coat them in flour, then beaten eggs, then breadcrumbs.
instructions.9: Heat oil in a pan and fry the croquettes until golden brown on all sides.
instructions.10: Drain the croquettes on paper towels to remove excess oil.

w-es-009.culturalNotes: Croquettes are a popular dish in Spain, often served as appetizers in bars and cafes.

w-es-010.title: Leche Frita

instructions.1: Add 3 cups of milk to a saucepan, along with a cinnamon stick and 4 lemon peels. Heat the mixture over medium heat until it comes to a light boil, then turn off the heat.
instructions.2: While the milk is infusing, add 1 cup of milk to a bowl and gradually add the corn starch while whisking continuously.
instructions.3: Grease a 10-inch by 6-inch casserole dish with 1 teaspoon of sunflower oil.
instructions.4: After 20 minutes of infusing, remove the lemon peels and cinnamon stick, then heat the milk over medium heat. Add the milk and corn starch mixture and granulated sugar gradually while whisking continuously for 20-25 minutes until the mixture becomes thick and creamy.
instructions.5: Transfer the thickened mixture to the greased casserole dish, let it cool, then cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
instructions.6: After a couple of hours, remove the casserole dish from the fridge, place a cutting board over the casserole, and invert it to easily remove the mixture. Cut the mixture into 1.5-inch by 1.5-inch squares.
instructions.7: Add corn starch to one bowl and beat the eggs in another. Coat each square of the mixture in corn starch, then in the egg wash, and place them on a plate lined with parchment paper.
instructions.8: Heat a small frying pan over medium heat and add 1/2 cup of sunflower oil. After 4 minutes, add the coated squares to the pan in a single layer, cooking in batches for 45-60 seconds per side. Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels.
instructions.9: Add granulated sugar and cinnamon powder to a bowl, and coat the fried squares in the mixture. Place them on a serving dish and sprinkle with lemon zest, then serve immediately.

w-es-010.culturalNotes: Leche Frita is a traditional Spanish dessert often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-es-011.title: Natillas (Spanish Vanilla Pudding)

instructions.1: Crack 3 organic eggs into a bowl and beat them, then add half of the sugar to the eggs and mix well, set aside.
instructions.2: Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat and add 2 1/4 cups of organic milk, the remaining sugar, 1 cinnamon stick, 1 vanilla bean, and 3 lemon peels. Mix everything together until it starts to boil gently, then lower the heat to low.
instructions.3: Add about 1/3 cup of the hot milk from the pan to the bowl with the eggs while continuing to mix, this will bring the egg mixture to the same temperature as the milk in the pan.
instructions.4: Before adding the egg mixture to the pan, remove the cinnamon stick, vanilla bean, and lemon peels.
instructions.5: Start slowly pouring the egg mixture into the pan while continuing to whisk the milk in the pan. Once all the egg mixture is in the pan, continue to whisk without stopping for about 3-4 minutes until a creamy texture forms, then turn off the heat and continue to whisk for another minute.
instructions.6: Transfer the creamy mixture into 3 small bowls, then sprinkle some cinnamon powder on top and add one Maria cookie on top of each bowl.
instructions.7: Cover each bowl with plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours.
instructions.8: Enjoy!

w-es-011.culturalNotes: Natillas is a traditional Spanish dessert usually served on special occasions.

w-es-012.title: Spanish Almond Nougat - Turron de Alicante

instructions.1: Preheat the oven to 210C (410F) with the bake/broil option.
instructions.2: Add 1 1/2 cups of blanched almonds to a baking tray lined with foil paper, spread the almonds in a single layer, and bake for 11-12 minutes. Remove from the oven and transfer to a bowl.
instructions.3: Reserve 1 egg white in a bowl and set aside at room temperature.
instructions.4: Heat a large frying pan over LOW heat and add 1/2 cup of honey. Cook for 15 minutes without stirring, then add 1/2 cup of white sugar and mix with the honey. Cook for another 15 minutes while continuing to gently mix without stopping.
instructions.5: Once you hit the 30-minute mark of cooking the honey and sugar, add the egg whites to an electric mixer and whisk at medium power until soft peaks form. Continue to cook and mix the honey sauce on LOW heat while doing this. Once soft peaks form, start slowly adding the hot caramel sauce in spoonfuls into the mixer until all the sauce in the pan is in the mixer. Continue to whisk for another 3 minutes.
instructions.6: Add the toasted almonds to the bowl with the nougat and mix with a spatula until everything is well combined.
instructions.7: Transfer the almond nougat into a bread pan that is 2 x 6 or 3 x 8 inches, make sure it’s lined with parchment paper.
instructions.8: You have two options: you can leave your almond nougat to sit overnight to harden up, or add it to a preheated oven with the BAKE only option at 70C (165F) for 2 hours, then let it rest for 1-2 hours before serving.

w-es-012.culturalNotes: Spanish nougat, known as Turron de Alicante, is a traditional sweet made in the region of Alicante, Spain.

w-es-013.title: Pa amb tomàquet (Bread with garlic & tomato)

instructions.1: Toast the bread slices under the broiler or on a hot grill for about 30 seconds per side.
instructions.2: Bring the toasted bread to the table. Give everyone a garlic clove to rub onto their toasted bread.
instructions.3: Rub the tomato halves on the toasted bread.
instructions.4: Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and freshly cracked pepper to taste.
instructions.5: Serve warm.

w-es-013.culturalNotes: Pa amb tomàquet is a traditional Catalan dish served as an appetizer or light meal.

w-es-014.title: Alicante Style Patatas Bravas

instructions.1: Pre-heat your oven with the bake/broil option to its highest setting.
instructions.2: Finely mince 1 clove of garlic and 1 small dried cayenne pepper.
instructions.3: Heat a small saucepan over medium heat and add 1 tablespoon of extra virgin Spanish olive oil.
instructions.4: Once the oil gets hot, add the minced garlic and minced cayenne pepper, mix for 15 seconds, then add 1 cup of tomato puree, 1/2 teaspoon of smoked paprika, a pinch of white sugar, and season with sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper. Mix everything together and lower the heat to LOW.
instructions.5: Thinly slice 1 large Yukon Gold potato into rounds about 1/16 inch thick.
instructions.6: Arrange the potato slices on a baking tray lined with parchment paper in a single layer, drizzle each slice with a bit of extra virgin Spanish olive oil, and season with sea salt.
instructions.7: Place the tray in the oven and bake for 20 minutes until the potatoes are cooked.
instructions.8: Once the potatoes are cooked, place the slices in a serving dish, pour the tomato mixture over the potatoes, and garnish with fresh parsley.

w-es-014.culturalNotes: Patatas Bravas is a popular dish in Spain, especially in the Alicante region, where it is served as a tapa in bars and cafes.

w-es-015.title: Spanish Pisto Andaluz

w-es-015-i2.name: potato
w-es-015-i2.standardAmount: 1 medium potato (peeled and cut into small cubes)

instructions.1: Heat a large fry pan over medium heat and add the olive oil.
instructions.2: In the meantime, cut the potato into small bite-sized cubes.
instructions.3: Once the oil is hot, add the chopped potato and mix to coat them in the olive oil, then stir every 3-4 minutes to ensure even frying.
instructions.4: While the potatoes are frying, roughly chop the onion and garlic, finely chop the bell peppers and zucchini, and finely grate the tomatoes.
instructions.5: After frying the potatoes for about 20 minutes until they are golden brown, remove them from the pan and set aside, making sure to reserve the olive oil in the pan.
instructions.6: Using the same pan, lower the heat to medium-low, add the chopped onion, garlic, and bell peppers, mix together, then stir every 1-2 minutes.
instructions.7: After 6-8 minutes and the vegetables are lightly sautéed, add the chopped zucchini, mix together, then stir every minute or so.
instructions.8: Once the zucchini is lightly sautéed, about 4 minutes, add the paprika and cumin, quickly mix together, then add the grated tomatoes, the fried potatoes, and season with salt and pepper, mix together, then simmer for 5-10 minutes or until the grated tomatoes have slightly thickened.
instructions.9: Transfer the mixture to a large serving dish and garnish with fresh parsley, enjoy!

w-es-015.culturalNotes: Spanish Pisto Andaluz is a traditional Spanish dish served as a main or side dish, featuring a mix of sautéed and fried vegetables.

w-es-016.title: Rice Pudding

instructions.1: In a medium pot, bring the water to a boil.
instructions.2: Add the rice, salt, cinnamon stick, and lemon zest. Cover and simmer for 16 minutes or until the rice is tender.
instructions.3: In a large pot, add the milk and sugar and cook until the mixture is hot and the sugar dissolves when whisked.
instructions.4: Stir a few spoonfuls of the hot milk mixture into the egg yolks to temper them.
instructions.5: Add the tempered egg yolks back into the hot milk mixture and whisk to combine.
instructions.6: Add the cooked rice (with the cinnamon stick and lemon zest) to the milk mixture. Cook at a gentle simmer until thickened enough to stand a spoon up into it. This takes about 35-40 minutes.
instructions.7: Garnish with cinnamon, lemon zest, raisins, and slivered almonds.

w-es-016.culturalNotes: Rice pudding is a traditional dessert in Spain, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-es-017.title: Spanish Potato Omelette

instructions.1: Peel the potatoes, wash them, and dry them with a cloth. Cut them into 1 cm cubes or 2 mm slices. Wash and dry them again. Add some salt to taste and mix them.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a pan. When hot, fry the potatoes but do not let them get brown. Once they're done, drain the oil and store the potatoes.
instructions.3: Dice or slice the onion; fry it until it is translucent.
instructions.4: Beat the 8 eggs in a bowl with a small amount of salt until the mix is homogenous. Then, mix in the potatoes and the onion.
instructions.5: Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in an empty pan – you can use the previous pan after removing most of the oil.
instructions.6: Once the pan is hot, add the egg with the onion and the potatoes.
instructions.7: After 7-8 minutes, the bottom part should be done. Put the dish over the pan and carefully turn it around so that the undone part rests on the dish. This is the most difficult step of the recipe. After that, put the pan on the fire again and slowly slide the mix into the pan to cook the other side.
instructions.8: After a couple of additional minutes, it should be done and ready to serve.

w-es-017.culturalNotes: The Spanish omelette is a traditional dish in Spain, also known as 'tortilla de patatas'. It is usually served as a light meal or as part of a lunch.

w-es-018.title: Tarta de Santiago

instructions.1: Add 350 grams of blanched almonds to a baking tray lined with parchment paper and place it in a preheated oven at 170°C (340°F) for 8-9 minutes until the almonds are lightly toasted.
instructions.2: Remove the almonds from the oven and let them cool, then add them to a food processor and grind for 35-45 seconds until you get small chunks, not powder.
instructions.3: In a large bowl, mix 250 grams of granulated sugar with 5 large eggs, then add 1 teaspoon of cinnamon powder and 1 teaspoon of lemon zest, and mix well.
instructions.4: Gradually add the almond mixture to the egg and sugar mixture, and continue mixing until all ingredients are well combined.
instructions.5: Line a 9-inch (22 cm) round baking pan with parchment paper and spray the sides with nonstick cooking spray, then add the cake mixture to the pan and tap it a few times on the counter to release any air bubbles and level the cake.
instructions.6: Place the baking pan in the preheated oven at 170°C (340°F) and bake for 55 minutes until the cake is fully cooked.
instructions.7: Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool, then remove it from the pan and transfer it to a serving dish.
instructions.8: Place the Saint James paper cut-out cross on the cake and sprinkle with powdered sugar, then gently remove the paper cross and serve the cake.

w-es-018.culturalNotes: Tarta de Santiago is a traditional almond cake from Galicia, Spain, and is often decorated with the Cross of St. James.

w-es-019.title: Spanish Scrambled Eggs with Zucchini | Zarangollo Murciano

instructions.1: Crack 4 eggs into a bowl, season with sea salt and black pepper, and lightly whisk the eggs for about 10 seconds, leaving some streaks of egg whites.
instructions.2: Thinly slice 1/2 onion.
instructions.3: Peel 1 medium-sized zucchini and cut it into rounds about 1/8 inch thick.
instructions.4: Heat a large nonstick fry pan over medium-high heat and add 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil.
instructions.5: After 1 minute, add the sliced onion and mix with the olive oil. After 2 minutes, add the sliced zucchini and continue to mix. Cook for 5-6 minutes until the zucchini is translucent and developing a light golden color and the onions are caramelized.
instructions.6: Reduce the heat to low-medium, add the egg mixture, and mix every 30 seconds. Cook until the eggs form large chunks, about 3 minutes, or until fully cooked. Remove the pan from the heat.
instructions.7: Transfer the mixture to a serving dish and sprinkle with freshly chopped chives. Enjoy!

w-es-019.culturalNotes: Zarangollo Murciano is a traditional dish from the Murcia region in Spain, known for its simplicity and rich flavor.

w-kr-001.title: Dol Sot Bibimbap (Korean Rice Dish)

instructions.1: Combine soy sauce, white sugar, brown sugar, minced garlic, chopped green onion, and toasted sesame seeds in a large bowl. Add sliced beef strips to the marinade and season with salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Bring rice and water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and cover; simmer until rice is tender and liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes.
instructions.3: Preheat the oven to 220 degrees C. Place 6 Korean stone bowls in the oven.
instructions.4: Combine shiitake mushrooms and 1/2 cup hot water in a small bowl; soak until pliable, about 10 minutes. Trim off and discard stems. Thinly slice caps and set aside.
instructions.5: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil. Add spinach to water just long enough to wilt leaves, then drain and pat dry. Set aside.
instructions.6: Combine cucumber and carrots in a bowl; season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
instructions.7: Preheat a wok over medium-high heat.
instructions.8: Cook and stir carrots and cucumbers in a small amount of sesame oil in the wok until softened. Remove from the wok and set aside. Add a small amount of sesame oil to the wok; cook and stir spinach in sesame oil for 1 to 2 minutes. Remove spinach from the wok and set aside. Add meat strips and marinade to the wok; cook, stirring frequently, until liquid reduces in volume, about 4 to 5 minutes.
instructions.9: Transfer the stone bowls from the oven to a suitable heat-resistant surface. Brush each bowl with sesame oil to coat. Divide rice into the bowls and gently pack to the bottom (the rice should sizzle as you arrange). Arrange cucumbers, carrots, bean sprouts, spinach, shiitake mushrooms, and beef mixture over each portion of rice.
instructions.10: Add one fried egg to each bowl, drizzle with 1 tablespoon sesame oil, and top with nori. Serve Kochujang sauce as a condiment.

w-kr-001.culturalNotes: Dol Sot Bibimbap is a traditional Korean dish served in hot stone bowls. The ingredients are mixed with rice before eating.

w-kr-002.title: Bibimbap

instructions.1: Cut the carrots into matchstick-sized strips.
instructions.2: Boil the strips in a covered pot of salted water for a few minutes. Drain.
instructions.3: Rinse the carrots with cold water until cool. Drain again, then put in a bowl.
instructions.4: Add the sesame oil, ground sesame seeds, grated garlic, and salt. Toss together with your fingers.

w-kr-002.culturalNotes: Bibimbap is a traditional Korean dish typically served with rice and a variety of vegetables.

w-kr-003.title: Bingsu with Sweet Red Beans

instructions.1: If using a special round container for the ice, fill it with water and put it in the freezer to make ice.
instructions.2: Open cans, clean berries, and prepare each of the toppings.
instructions.3: Slice strawberries.
instructions.4: Shave the ice into a large bowl that can hold all the ingredients.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the roasted grains powder on the ice using a small sieve.
instructions.6: Add berries and mini mochi rice cake.
instructions.7: Spoon the sweet red beans on top or on the side, then drizzle the sweetened condensed milk.

w-kr-003.culturalNotes: Bingsu is a traditional Korean dessert served in the summer, consisting of shaved ice with fruits and sweet toppings.

w-kr-004.title: Hobak Bokkeum (Stir-Fried Zucchini)

instructions.1: Cut the summer squash into 6 mm thick slices, then cut into equal sizes. If using Korean round squash, cut into quarters. If using common long zucchini, cut into half circles.
instructions.2: Chop the fermented shrimp until it is finely ground. When scooping out the shrimp from the jar, try to take out the shrimp but not the brine.
instructions.3: In a bowl, add the sliced squash and chopped fermented shrimp and mix gently. Let it sit for 30 minutes, turning over 2-3 times during this period.
instructions.4: While you wait, chop the garlic, fresh red chili pepper, and green onions.
instructions.5: In a frying pan over medium-high heat, sauté the garlic in perilla or sesame oil until it starts to bubble but not brown (less than a minute).
instructions.6: Add the squash and any liquid that has collected in the bowl to the frying pan, along with the water. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes over medium-high to medium heat until the zucchini is slightly crunchy but soft.
instructions.7: Right before turning off the heat, add the chopped green onions and sliced fresh red chili pepper (if using).
instructions.8: Transfer the stir-fried Hobak Bokkeum to a large plate or tray and spread it out to cool quickly. Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Cooling the bokkeum quickly helps to keep its vibrant green color.

w-kr-004.culturalNotes: Stir-fried bokkeum is a popular Korean side dish, typically served with warm rice.

w-kr-005.title: Crispy Zucchini Pancakes (Hobak Buchimgae)

instructions.1: Cut the Korean zucchini into 1/4 inch slices and then into matchsticks. One zucchini should make about 2 cups.
instructions.2: Peel and slice the onion into thin slices, similar thickness as the zucchini.
instructions.3: Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of sea salt over the zucchini sticks and toss them. Make sure the salt is evenly distributed. Leave them salted for 5-7 minutes.
instructions.4: Gently squeeze out excess water from the zucchini sticks.
instructions.5: In a large bowl, add the zucchini sticks, sliced onions, flour, water, and tempura mix. Mix gently until fully combined. The consistency should be like pancake batter or drinkable yogurt.
instructions.6: Heat a non-stick frying pan or cast iron pan on medium-high heat with about 1-2 tablespoons of oil.
instructions.7: Fry the pancake until the edges turn brown. This should take about 3 minutes on each side.
instructions.8: Flip the pancake when the bottom side edges turn golden brown.
instructions.9: Add more oil (1 tablespoon or more) after flipping the pancake.
instructions.10: When both sides are browned, move the pancake to a cutting board and cut it into bite-sized pieces.
instructions.11: Serve the pancake hot with a soy sauce and vinegar dipping sauce.

w-kr-005.culturalNotes: Hobak Buchimgae is a type of crispy Korean pancake made from zucchini. It is typically served as an appetizer or part of a breakfast meal.

w-kr-006.title: Budae-jjigae (Korean Army Base Stew)

instructions.1: Divide the fully cooked halal chicken luncheon meat into two piles on either side of a stock pot; layer the sausage, onion, and kimchi on top, leaving an empty space in the center of the pot.
instructions.2: Combine the Korean red pepper powder, gochujang, soy sauce, garlic, and black pepper in a small bowl; pour into the center of the pot. Sprinkle in the green onions and pour in the chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally until the flavors combine.
instructions.3: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the ramen noodles and cook, stirring until partially cooked and softened, about 2 minutes. Drain and transfer to the pot with the meat-kimchi mixture. Cook and stir until the ramen noodles are tender but firm to the bite, about 5 minutes. Top the stew with the cheese.

w-kr-006.culturalNotes: Budae-jjigae is a traditional Korean stew that originated in the post-Korean War era, using ingredients available from U.S. military bases.

w-kr-007.title: Fried Kelp Chips (Dasima Bugak)

instructions.1: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or fryer.
instructions.2: While the oil is heating, wipe both sides of the kelp sheet with a wet towel to remove any extra salt residue.
instructions.3: Cut the kelp sheet into 1.5 x 1.5 inch squares using scissors.
instructions.4: Prepare a plate lined with paper towels or a fryer basket next to the fryer.
instructions.5: When the oil is heated enough (150°C/300°F), throw in a handful of kelp pieces and start frying. The kelp pieces should balloon or flower in just seconds. When they have floated to the top, leave them to fry a couple more seconds and using a spider or a fryer basket, take them out onto the prepared plate.
instructions.6: Once it’s cooled a little, sprinkle sugar generously on both sides.

w-kr-007.culturalNotes: Fried kelp chips (Dasima Bugak) are a popular snack in South Korea, typically served as an appetizer or light snack.

w-kr-008.title: Chong Gak Kimchi (Chong Gak Kimchi)

instructions.1: Wash the young radish and clean off excess dirt and roots. It works best if you scrape the outside with the edge of a knife. Clean the edges where the root part ends and the green stems start. Cut off any yellow leaves or stems and the outer greens if they look tough. Cut off the pointy root ends of the radish.
instructions.2: Get a large bowl. Salt the radish evenly by layering the radish and salting each layer as you go. Evenly spread out 1/4 cup of salt throughout. Sprinkle 1 cup of water on top of the salted radish. Gently turn the radish and salt water to make sure it gets an even coating of the salt and water. DO NOT handle the radish too much because it can bring out a grassy taste from the kimchi. Let it sit about 2 hours. In hot weather, 1 1/2 hrs should be sufficient. About halfway through, turn the radish once making sure every radish is salted properly.
instructions.3: Wash and clean green onions (about a handful or 2 bunches). Cut some of the thicker root ends in half and then cut green onions into 2 in long pieces.
instructions.4: Prepare the flour paste: Mix 1 Tbsp of flour with 1 cup of water until smooth.
instructions.5: Prepare the seasoning (yangnyum): Mix 3/4 cup of Korean red chili powder, 3 Tbsp of chopped garlic, 2 Tbsp of chopped ginger, 1/4 cup of fermented anchovy liquid, 1-2 Tbsp of sugar, and a pinch of salt (if needed).
